# v0.11.0 Correctness Plan — implement-ready (rev 2, post-adversarial-review)

Audit of v0.10.0 (`b8ff9a5`) found 6 critical, ~12 major, ~20 minor defects. This plan
fixes all criticals + majors + cheap minors, defers the rest (see §Deferred). Version is
**v0.11.0**, not v0.10.1: generated files change shape (gate exit codes, wrapper, agent
frontmatter) — same MINOR rationale the v0.10.0 CHANGELOG entry states.

Rev 2: an adversarial review verified every anchor and premise against the repo; this
revision incorporates all its fixes (pure-copy inventory, span-marker preservation,
heredoc removal, dead anchors, contract mismatches).

## Ground rules for the implementer

1. **Anchor-verify before every edit.** Each task quotes an exact anchor string. `grep -n`
   the anchor in the named file first; if it is missing or matches more than once where the
   task assumes uniqueness, STOP and re-read the file — do not guess. Line numbers in this
   plan are v0.10.0 hints only; anchors are authoritative. Template paths like
   `templates/...` and `hook-templates/...` are relative to `skills/espalier-init/`.
2. **Portability bar:** bash 3.2 (macOS default) — no `declare -A`, no `${var,,}`, no
   `mapfile`; BSD + GNU sed (no bare `sed -i`; follow the existing branched pattern in
   `scripts/migrate-v0.3-to-v0.4.sh:72-77`); BSD + GNU grep (no `grep -P`).
3. **Claude Code hook semantics (the fact behind Workstream A):** for `PreToolUse` and
   `PostToolUse` hooks, ONLY exit code 2 blocks/feeds-back, and the message must be on
   **stderr**. Exit 1 + stdout is a silent no-op. Git-hook semantics (any non-zero blocks)
   do NOT apply — these scripts are wired in `.claude/settings.json`, not `.git/hooks/`.
4. **Order:** Workstreams A → C → B → F → D → E → G. E6 (the new migration script) copies
   spans from files A/C produce, so it must come after them. G (docs) last.
5. **After each workstream:** run `bash scripts/test-hooks.sh` and
   `bash scripts/test-bootstrap.sh`; both must pass before moving on.
6. Repo rule: commits use Conventional Commits, **no co-author trailer**.

## Workstream A — hook exit-code semantics (CRITICAL: the push gate currently never blocks)

### A1. pre-push-gate.sh: every block path → exit 2 + stderr
**File:** `skills/espalier-init/hook-templates/pre-push-gate.sh`
**Defect:** all 8 blocking paths are `exit 1` with `echo` to stdout (v0.10.0 lines 77, 95,
131, 140, 180, 191, 209, 226). As a PreToolUse hook this never blocks the push.
**Change:**
- For every `BLOCKED` path: redirect the echo group to stderr and `exit 2`. Pattern:
  ```sh
  {
    echo "BLOCKED: Pipeline is at Stage $CURRENT_STAGE (need ≥ 7 for push)"
    echo "Complete code review and tests before pushing."
  } >&2
  exit 2
  ```
  Apply to all 8 sites (find them with `grep -n 'exit 1' hook-templates/pre-push-gate.sh`).
- Every `WARNING:` echo also goes to stderr (`>&2`) with exit 0 unchanged — warnings on
  stdout are invisible in hook context.
- Update the header comment block (anchor: `Never affects the exit code.`) to document:
  "Blocking paths exit 2 with the reason on stderr — Claude Code PreToolUse semantics;
  exit 1 would NOT block."
**Verify:** after A1 alone, `grep -c 'exit 2' hook-templates/pre-push-gate.sh` = 8 and
`grep -c 'exit 1'` = 0. (A3 later adds 2 more blocking paths; the end-of-workstream
totals are asserted in A6: exit-2 count = 10, exit-1 count = 0.)

### A2. Secret scan runs even with no in-flight change — WITHOUT breaking migration span markers
**File:** same.
**Defect:** anchor `WARNING: No in-flight Espalier change found.` exits 0 *before* the
secret scan, so any between-pipelines manual push skips it — contradicting the design
comment `A leaked credential must fail closed`.
**Constraint (do not violate):** `scripts/migrate-v0.9.1-to-v0.9.2.sh` and
`scripts/migrate-v0.9.6-to-v0.10.0.sh` extract spans FROM THIS TEMPLATE using
column-0 line anchors — `^# Run tests and check count` and `^echo "All gates passed` among
them. Those markers must remain at column 0, and every extracted span must stay
syntactically self-contained (no `if` opened outside a span closing inside it).
**Change:**
- The no-state-file branch must NOT `exit 0`: set `PIPELINE_TRACKED=no`, emit the warning
  (stderr), and continue.
- Move each pipeline-only gate's body (build check, lint check, test-count check) into a
  named function defined next to `run_build`/`run_lint`/`run_tests` — e.g.
  `gate_tests_section() { …existing body unchanged… }` — and at the original site call it
  behind a single-line guard:
  ```sh
  if [ "$PIPELINE_TRACKED" = "yes" ]; then gate_tests_section; fi
  ```
  Use the `if …; then …; fi` form, NOT `[ … ] && …` — the latter returns non-zero when the
  guard is false, which `set -e` treats as failure. The `^# Run tests and check count`
  marker comment and the `^echo "All gates passed` line stay untouched at column 0, and no
  `if` may open outside an extraction span and close inside one — the span-integrity check
  in Verify (2) is the proof.
- The stage check and certificate check (not span-extracted — confirm with
  `grep -n 'Current Stage\|Reviewed-Diff' scripts/migrate-v0.9.*.sh scripts/migrate-v0.9.6-to-v0.10.0.sh`
  before assuming) may use a plain `if [ "$PIPELINE_TRACKED" = "yes" ]; then … fi` wrapper.
- The secret scan + dependency audit run unconditionally (they already handle the
  no-Base-Ref case via upstream / `HEAD~1` fallback), then `exit 0`.
**Verify:** (1) fixture: scratch repo, TWO commits (so `HEAD~1` exists), no
`espalier/changes/` state, no gitleaks installed, fake AWS key (`AKIA` + 16
uppercase/digits) added in the second commit → gate exits 2 with `BLOCKED: a possible
hard-coded secret` on stderr; repeat with gitleaks installed if available. (2) span
integrity: `bash -n` passes on the template AND on the output of the span extraction used
by `scripts/migrate-v0.9.6-to-v0.10.0.sh` (run its extraction function against the new
template in a scratch dir); the two column-0 markers still match `^# Run tests and check
count` and `^echo "All gates passed`.

### A3. Corrupt/hand-edited state file must fail closed
**File:** same.
**Defect:** missing `Current Stage:` line ⇒ stage check silently skipped; missing
`Base-Ref:`/`Reviewed-Diff:` ⇒ certificate check downgraded to a warning. Deleting two
lines from `pipeline-state.md` neutralizes both gates.
**Change:**
- Stage check (anchor `CURRENT_STAGE=$(grep "Current Stage:"`): if `CURRENT_STAGE` is
  empty while `PIPELINE_TRACKED=yes` → BLOCK (exit 2, stderr): `BLOCKED: pipeline-state.md
  has no parsable 'Current Stage:' line — state file corrupt or hand-edited.`
- Certificate check (anchor `WARNING: No review certificate`): keep the legacy allowance
  ONLY when the state file's Stage History contains no `| 4 | PASSED` row (true legacy);
  if a Stage-4 PASSED row exists but `Base-Ref`/`Reviewed-Diff` are missing → BLOCK
  (exit 2, stderr) with `BLOCKED: Stage 4 passed but the review certificate is missing`.
**Verify:** covered by A6 cases 4-5; per-file totals after A3: `grep -c 'exit 2'` = 10,
`grep -c 'exit 1'` = 0.

### A4. pre-push-gate-wrapper.sh: fail-closed python fallback + broader match
**File:** `skills/espalier-init/hook-templates/pre-push-gate-wrapper.sh`
**Defect (two):** (a) `python3 … 2>/dev/null` — python3 absent ⇒ `COMMAND` empty ⇒ exit 0,
gate silently bypassed. (b) `case` patterns miss `git -C /path push`, multi-line commands
(`npm test\ngit push`), double spaces.
**Change:** replace the extract-and-case block (anchor: `COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | python3`)
with:
```sh
INPUT=$(cat)

# Documented escape hatch.
[ -n "${ESPALIER_SKIP_GATE:-}" ] && exit 0

# Fast path: if the raw hook JSON doesn't even contain "git" and "push",
# this is not a push — allow without needing python at all.
if ! printf '%s' "$INPUT" | grep -q 'git' || ! printf '%s' "$INPUT" | grep -q 'push'; then
  exit 0
fi

PYBIN=""
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && PYBIN=python3
[ -z "$PYBIN" ] && command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && PYBIN=python
if [ -z "$PYBIN" ]; then
  # Cannot parse the command reliably and it plausibly contains a push: fail CLOSED.
  echo "BLOCKED: espalier push gate cannot run — python3 not found (needed to parse the hook input). Install python3, or bypass once with ESPALIER_SKIP_GATE=1." >&2
  exit 2
fi
COMMAND=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | "$PYBIN" -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('tool_input',{}).get('command',''))") \
  || { echo "BLOCKED: espalier push gate could not parse hook input JSON." >&2; exit 2; }

# Match a real `git push` invocation anywhere in the (possibly multi-line,
# possibly `git -C dir push`) command. Strip quoted SPANS first (not whole lines)
# so `echo "git push"` doesn't trigger but `git commit -m "git push docs" && git push`
# still does.
STRIPPED=$(printf '%s\n' "$COMMAND" | sed -E "s/\"[^\"]*\"//g; s/'[^']*'//g")
if printf '%s\n' "$STRIPPED" \
   | grep -qE '(^|[;&|[:space:]])git([[:space:]]+(-C[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+|--?[[:alnum:]][^[:space:]]*))*[[:space:]]+push([[:space:]]|$)'; then
  # …existing repo-root dispatch unchanged, except the `cannot cd` error path
  # becomes: message >&2; exit 2.
  :
fi
exit 0
```
(The `:` marks where the existing dispatch body goes — keep it verbatim apart from the
exit-2 change.) Apply the same PYBIN probe to `post-edit-wrapper.sh` (anchor `python3 -c`),
but there, python absence ⇒ exit 0 (post-edit is advisory, not a gate) — no fail-closed.
**Verify:** A6 wrapper matrix, 6 cases: plain `git push` (blocked-path dispatch reached);
`git -C /tmp/x push`; multi-line `npm test\ngit push`; `echo "git push"` (must NOT
dispatch); `git commit -m "git push docs" && git push` (MUST dispatch); python3+python
absent (simulate with PATH stripped) → exit 2.

**Files:** `hook-templates/check-layer-boundaries-typescript.sh`, `-python.sh`, `-go.sh`
**Defect:** `LAYER VIOLATION` printed to stdout with exit 1 — invisible as PostToolUse.

**Verify:** for EACH of the three files: `grep -c 'exit 2'` ≥ 1 AND `grep -c 'exit 1'` = 0.

  (6) the 6-case wrapper matrix from A4. Follow the suite's existing red-first convention.
**Verify:** `bash scripts/test-hooks.sh` exits 0; assertion count grows by ≥ 12.

## Workstream B — orchestrator/lane logic (B2 first; other B tasks touch the same regions)

### B2. Verdict gate: gate on the verdict WORD + detect ESCALATION_REQUIRED everywhere
**Files:** `templates/skills/espalier.md`, `templates/skills/espalier-fix.md`,
`templates/pipeline.md`. (`espalier-review.md` / `espalier-security.md` verdict
DEFINITIONS are covered by C3 — no B2 edit there.)
**Defect:** Stage 4/6 gates parse only `p0=`. `VERDICT: FAIL p0=0 p1=1` and
`VERDICT: ESCALATION_REQUIRED p0=0` both advance as PASS. ESCALATION_REQUIRED is only
detected at fix-lane Stage 6.
**Change — one canonical gate paragraph, written once and copied verbatim into each gate
site** (espalier.md Stage 4 gate steps 3-5, anchor `Gate read (deterministic)`;
espalier-fix.md Stage 4 gate steps 3-4, anchor `Gate read: `; both lanes' Stage 6
test-review gates; pipeline.md Stage 4 + Stage 6 summaries):

> **Gate read (deterministic).** From EACH record:
> `V=$(grep '^VERDICT:' <record> | tail -1)`. Parse the verdict WORD and the counts.
> - `ESCALATION_REQUIRED` (either agent, either lane, any stage) → do NOT advance and do
>   NOT re-spawn: snapshot the sentinel, then run the escalation protocol (fix lane: the
>   late-escalation prompt; full lane: escalate to the human with the agent's Escalation
>   Reason block). An `ESCALATION_REQUIRED` with `p0=0` is still an escalation.
> - Verdict word `FAIL`, or `p0=` > 0, or `p1=` > 0 → re-spawn `harness-coder` with the
>   combined findings and loop (counter + `max-code-rounds` cap unchanged).
> - Advance ONLY when EVERY record's last sentinel has verdict word `PASS` or
>   `PASS_WITH_FIXES` AND `p0=0` AND `p1=0` on the current code.

Update the two summary lines that currently say "Only when BOTH sentinels read p0=0"
(espalier.md anchor `Only when BOTH sentinels read p0=0`; pipeline.md equivalent) to
"Only when both last sentinels are PASS/PASS_WITH_FIXES with p0=0 p1=0".
`PASS_WITH_FIXES` retains its meaning: only P2/P3 notes remain.
**Verify:** `grep -c 'Advance ONLY when EVERY record' skills/espalier-init/templates/skills/espalier.md
skills/espalier-init/templates/skills/espalier-fix.md skills/espalier-init/templates/pipeline.md`

2. `grep -rn 'exit 1' skills/espalier-init/hook-templates/*.sh` returns no blocking-path
   hits (only non-gate helpers, if any).
3. Fresh init on a scratch TypeScript repo: Stage 11 all 46 checks pass; symlinks
   relative; simulated `git push` at Stage 3 is BLOCKED (wrapper/gate exit 2, message on
   stderr).
4. Migration chain from a v0.10.0 fixture reaches "Already fully up to date" on second
   run; pre-v0.9.2 chain regression (E6 verify 2) passes.
5. Phantom-reference sweep: every state field/section a skill READS
   (`Files likely touched`, `Layers involved`, `Status: ESCALATED`, `FILED`,
   `caused_by`, `Review Rounds`, `## Open Questions`) is WRITTEN by an instruction in the
   same or an upstream file — grep each name for both a read site and a write site.
